thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Stripe kube-proxy reports increased 5xx/429 rates from webhook verification path /webhook/receive. Paging oncall for billing-impacting errors. root_ts=1776345678

Sara H: Im taking this. Alerts show 429 spikes to Stripe when we call invoice fetch endpoints. Started ~07:02 UTC. Customers hitting limited-mode flags.

AJ Patel: Logs show Stripe responses with headers like:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
Stripe-Rate-Limit-Reset: 120
{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded"}}
```
We also see occasional 502s proxied back to us.

Devon: Are inbound webhooks failing to reach us, or is it our outbound calls to Stripe that are 429ing?

Luis_ops: Quick summary: Stripe sent a burst of events (looks like a reconciliation job). Our webhook consumer immediately fetches invoice details for each event and that burst pushed our outbound quota against Stripe. Stripe started returning 429s which prevents invoice confirm -> billing enforcement stalls. Impact: some users in limited-mode; not a total outage but business-impacting.

Maria_support: CX: 12 tickets created so far, two enterprise accounts flagged for missing invoices. Drafting comms.

Sara H: Mitigation plan (short):
- Flip to polling fallback to reconcile recent events rather than real-time per-webhook fetch.
- Increase entitlement_cache TTL to avoid immediate limited-mode toggles.
- Reduce outbound concurrency and add jitter/backoff for Stripe API calls.
- Open Stripe support ticket and ping AM.

AJ Patel: Polling prototype (to be rolled via feature flag stripe.polling.fallback):
```
# pseudo-code
start = now - 3600
for acct in active_accounts:
  events = stripe.events.list(limit=100, created_gte=start)
  for e in events: process_event(e)
  sleep(0.2) # global throttle
```
We will shard across workers and cap per-account QPS.

Devon: Kicking off canary deploy at 07:15 UTC (5% traffic). Canary includes: polling.fallback=on, webhook handler concurrency 12, cache_ttl=900s.

incident-bot: Deploy started by @Devon  Canary 5% at 07:15 UTC.

Luis_ops: Also patching background reconciliation: reduce parallel workers from 40 -> 8 and wire exponential backoff for 429 responses. Pushed config change to staging.

Sara H: Maria, please prepare external status line referencing third-party rate-limiting; avoid naming internal quotas. CX note should say: "Were seeing delays in billing sync due to third-party (payment provider) rate limiting. Our team has enabled fallbacks; you may see payment status updates delayed up to 2 hours."

Maria_support: Will send at 07:30 UTC. Also attaching quick FAQ on how to request expedited reconciliation for impacted customers.

AJ Patel: Stripe ticket created INC-9012 and AM looped in. Sent sample request-ids and trace logs. They replied acknowledging unusual spike and recommended reducing concurrency + exponential backoff.

Devon: Canary metrics look stable. No new limited-mode reports in the canary cohort. Increasing to 30% at 07:28 UTC.

incident-bot: Canary increased to 30% by @Devon at 07:28 UTC.

Luis_ops: Noted that our signature verification path does a synchronous invoice fetch which is hot. We'll move to async verification for webhooks so we ack quickly and fetch details from polling workers. Patch queued.

Sara H: For handoff: set runbook pointers
- Current owner: Sara H
- Next oncall in 90m: @Luis_ops
- Mitigations live: polling.fallback=30%, cache_ttl=900s, webhook concurrency=12, background workers=8, backoff implemented
- Customer impact: degraded billing sync causing limited-mode for a subset; approx 12 tickets so far
- Escalation: Stripe AM engaged, ticket INC-9012

Devon: Rolling polling to 100% at 07:40 UTC. Monitoring ingestion lag and error rates.

incident-bot: polling.fallback toggled ON (100%) by @Devon at 07:40 UTC.

AJ Patel: Initial recovery note: outbound 429s dropped by 70% after concurrency/backoff changes and polling. Invoices are being reprocessed. Well keep polling enabled until Stripe confirms quota restored.

Maria_support: Posted status update and shared contact for urgent escalations. Added impacted accounts to a dedicated ticket queue for manual follow-up.

Luis_ops: Stripe AM updated: they had an internal job spike and applied aggressive rate-limiting; working on quota smoothing. They requested we avoid retry storms — they were seeing bursts from several integrators. Next update ETA 30m.

Sara H: Action items for post-incident:
- Add circuit-breaker for Stripe (circuit trips after X 429s per minute)
- Implement async webhook ack + deferred fetch
- Improve dashboards: per-account billing-staleness and Stripe 429s count
- Update runbook with polling fallback steps and customer comms template
Assigning postmortem owner: AJ Patel.

oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled: @Sara H -> @Luis_ops in 1 hour.

AJ Patel: Ill own the postmortem and timeline. Preliminary severity: SEV-2 due to customer-impacting billing delays.

Luis_ops: Taking over monitoring and Stripe follow-up. Will update thread on Stripes next ETA and whether we need to open account-level escalations.

Sara H: Thanks team. Good mitigation work, nice quick rollout. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Handoff complete at 08:50 UTC. New oncall: Luis_ops. Incident remains active until Stripe confirms quota normalization.
